title: The Terminal of the Rust Belt
premise: Edmund Dravenmoor smuggles forbidden memories through the decaying orbital stations of the Rust Belt while tending a beacon whose original owner—and purpose—have been erased from every record. When the beacon answers a distress call in a dead language, he learns it is a lock, and he is the key: the descendant of the engineer who split humanity's cryo-fleet in two rather than let one faction win the war that emptied Earth. The fleet's truce expires in ninety days, and both halves are converging on his station to claim the beacon's authorization codes. Torn between Mara, a customs officer who has been quietly falsifying his manifests for years, and the duty he never chose, Edmund finally decodes the beacon's true message: it can wake only half the sleepers, and it will accept the choice of whoever holds it at expiration. He ends the stalemate by broadcasting the choice itself—waking the sleepers in mixed lots, half from each faction, forcing the fleet to become one crew or lose everyone—and chooses, at last, to stop being invisible.
about_author: Ansel Brightwater is the pen name of a former shipping clerk who spent eleven years in Great Lakes freight yards before turning to science fiction. Their work dwells on rust, radio, and the people who maintain machines everyone else has forgotten.

chapters.title: Manifest of Small Ghosts
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A routine smuggling run through Meridian Station customs introduces his double life: contraband memories in one hold, beacon maintenance logs in the other. Mara Voss, customs officer, waves him through with a look that says she knows. Emotional beat: the loneliness of competence—Edmund is good at a job no one is supposed to notice.

chapters.title: The Language That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The beacon receives a burst transmission in pre-Exodus English dialect, dead for two centuries. Edmund's inherited decoder ring—his grandmother's 'heirloom junk'—partially translates it: a countdown and a word he renders as 'custodian.' Emotional beat: unease curdling into wonder; the past has his address.

chapters.title: Mara's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. We see the smuggling from the other side: her years of falsified manifests, her reasons, her growing fear that Edmund's beacon is now flagged by fleet intelligence. She warns him off-world. Emotional beat: love expressed as paperwork—protection disguised as bureaucracy.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Rust
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He traces the beacon's commissioning order to his own bloodline: his ancestor built it to hold the cryo-fleet's waking authorization after refusing to choose a victor in the Schism War. Emotional beat: the weight of an inheritance he never agreed to carry.

chapters.title: Two Banners, One Orbit
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both fleet factions arrive in the Rust Belt under truce flags, each claiming custodial rights. Station politics fracture; Edmund's neighbors who ignored him for decades now need him. Emotional beat: the vertigo of becoming important against your will.

chapters.title: What the Sleepers Dream
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Using smuggled memory-chips, Edmund experiences fragments of the sleepers' archived dreams and realizes both factions' frozen passengers are more mixed than their leaders admit. Emotional beat: grief for a divided humanity that was never as divided as its banners.

chapters.title: The Offer She Couldn't Refuse
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Fleet intelligence blackmails Mara into planting a tracker on the beacon, threatening to expose her falsifications and Edmund's smuggling. She complies, then confesses to Edmund. Emotional beat: love against duty—she chooses truth over safety and risks everything.

chapters.title: Expiration Date
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. With the truce hours from expiry, both factions demand the beacon's codes. Mara's betrayal is discovered; Edmund must decide whether to forgive her while physically wiring himself into the beacon as the final custodian. Emotional beat: the climax's terrible clarity—someone must choose, and it is him.

chapters.title: Half of Everyone
chapters.summary: Climax. Edmund refuses the binary, reprogramming the beacon to wake sleepers in mixed lots from both factions and broadcasting the fleet's true passenger manifests to every ship at once. The factions must cooperate or lose their people. Emotional beat: defiance as an act of love for strangers.

chapters.title: Beacon, Burning Visible
chapters.summary: Resolution. Weeks later, the fleet limps toward cooperation; mixed-crew salvage teams rebuild the Rust Belt. Edmund, no longer invisible, tends the beacon openly with Mara at his side, its light now a shared inheritance. Emotional beat: belonging earned not by choosing a side, but by refusing to let sides be the whole story.
